sources.citation: Stokhof, W. A. L. (ed.) 1983. Holle Lists: vocabularies in languages of Indonesia, Vol. 5/2: Irian Jaya: Papuan languages, Northern languages, Central Highlands languages. Pacific Linguistics D-53. Foya (= Mander/Jofotek per Usher) list 132b pp. 109-115.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Foya list is a bare Dutch-orthography wordlist with no accent marks and no note on accent (its sec. 1.2 only locates Biri/Foya). The note 'Accent is indicated by ' above the syllable' belongs to the separate Berrik Papua (Tor River/Berik) list intro, not to Foya.

sources.citation: Usher, Timothy. n.d. New Guinea World: Jofotek. newguineaworld.linguistik.uzh.ch/families/northwest-new-guinea/foja-range/orya-tor-river/tor-river/east-tor-river/jofotek
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Phonology section '[under construction]', empty. Only pronouns after Lee & Wambaliau 2004:50, which carry stress marks (aj, e'me, di'gan, aj-eme, eme-gan). Lists all known sources (Oosterwal 1961; Voorhoeve 1975:107; Stokhof 1983:108-115 Foya; Smits & Voorhoeve 1994; Lee & Wambaliau 2004:49-62) and states Jofotek = Oosterwal's Mander.

sources.citation: Badan Pengembangan dan Pembinaan Bahasa, Kementerian Pendidikan Dasar dan Menengah. n.d. Peta Bahasa: Bahasa di Provinsi Papua -- entries 'Juvutek' (idb=438: Kampung Komra, Distrik Pantai Timur, Kabupaten Sarmi), 'Srum' (idb=638: Kampung Tarontha Srum, Distrik Bonggo), 'Mander' (idb=524: etnik Buknes, Kampung Rotea, Distrik Bonggo; also spoken in Kampung Bu, Srum and Biri II) and 'Etik (Barto, Maria)' (idb=405: Kampung Komra (Biridua)). Online language-mapping database (petabahasa.kemendikdasmen.go.id), accessed 2026-09-20.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No phonology content: each entry gives speaker location, neighbouring languages as reported by residents, and a dialectometric difference percentage (Juvutek 99.50-99.75% vs Yokari, Molof etc; Srum 97.75-100% vs Sunum, Wakde; Mander 'bahasa tersendiri' vs Mawes, Marenggi, Vedan Nus). The underlying Badan Bahasa 400-item field wordlists are not published on the site.

sources.citation: Eberhard, David M. & Lucija Simicic [Šimičić]. 2026. Deferred Vernacular Production in the transmission of local languages: Preliminary evidence from Sãotomense, Angolar, Molise Croatian and beyond. Language Documentation & Conservation 20: 97-124.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No phonology at all. Sole relevant sentence (sec. on Prolonged Vernacular Acquisition): 'PVA has been reported in 15 languages so far.. and Kwesten, Keijar, Dabe, Vitou, Edwas, Tena, Kwinsu, Jofotek, Yamna, Fedan, and Korur in Indonesia (Peddie 2021).' Value for this hunt: it shows the unpublished Kwanem survey report's sociolinguistic findings reached Peddie 2021 (Edinburgh MSc) and thence print, i.e. the Lee & Wambaliau draft is obtainable through SIL survey circles.

sources.citation: Wurm, Stephen A. 2007. Australasia and the Pacific. In Christopher Moseley (ed.), Encyclopedia of the World's Endangered Languages, 425-577. London: Routledge.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: EWEL has no 'Jofotek' or 'Bromnya' entry (names coined by the 2005 SIL survey); the Mander [197] and Foya [7] entries describe the same upper Tor / Bu River speech community that Glottolog splits into mand1443 and jofo1235. Nothing on stress/tone.

sources.citation: Voorhoeve, C. L. 1975. Languages of Irian Jaya: Checklist. Preliminary classification, language maps, wordlists. Pacific Linguistics B-31. Entry 75 MANDER (IX a, +-100, village Matebefon); wordlist 75 p.107 after Anceaux.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No phonology; entry gives village and sources (Oosterwal 1961, Voorhoeve 1971) only; wordlist key p.92: 'Stress and pitch are not indicated.'

sources.citation: Voorhoeve, C. L. 1971. Miscellaneous notes on languages in West Irian, New Guinea. In T. Dutton, C. L. Voorhoeve & S. A. Wurm, Papers in New Guinea Linguistics No. 14, 47-114. Pacific Linguistics A-28. Canberra: Australian National University. DOI 10.15144/PL-A28.47. Section 2.3.5.1 'Tor Stock' (pp. 66-70): Tami-Tor lexicostatistics and probable-cognate sets using Oosterwal's (1961) eight Tor wordlists, including Mander (MA).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress, accent or tone for Mander or any Tor language. The Tor content is cognate percentages (Manem-Ittik 19%, Taikat-Berik 14%..), a list of probable Tami-Tor cognates with Mander forms respelled from Oosterwal (MA dzu 'bird', MA kerane 'bone', MA/IT suwe 'egg'..), and one segmental remark (p. 67, note under set 2 'bone'): 'In many words MA retains an initial k which has been lost in other Tor languages.' The paper's stress statements (the text layer 'Bi-syllabic words generally have stress on the last syllable..' and 2042-2043 'The place of the accent is not fixed..') are in sec…

sources.note: Nothing; jofo1235 has 0 descriptive refs; mand1443Glottolog's fullest description is only a wordlist (Oosterwal 1961, 14 pp; Stroeve 1911, 2 pp).
Nothing; stub: dialects Bromnya (Srum) and Jofotek (Biridua); 'Colonial records of Mander show it to be the same language.'

sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only linguist-collected material on Jofotek-Bromnya (239-item IPA wordlist + 21 sentences for Jofotek of Biridua, pp. 49-62, with stress marked; also Bromnya of Srum). Any transcription note or phonological remark on stress would be here; even without prose, the full stress-marked list would allow a data-based reading.
